claim: Microsoft reconfirmed in 2025 that the full Visual Studio IDE stays Windows-only; VS Code is the recommendation on Linux/macOS.
quote: Microsoft has reaffirmed that its full-featured Visual Studio IDE will remain exclusive to Windows... advises its Visual Studio developers to use Visual Studio Code on Linux and macOS machines.

claim: The native Teams desktop client for Linux was retired; the PWA is the supported path.
quote: Those currently using the Teams app on Linux need to transition to using the new progressive web app (PWA) which is now available or Teams on the web.

claim: Intune Linux management covers Ubuntu LTS with GNOME on corporate-owned devices only; compliance and conditional access flow through Intune, Entra ID and Edge.
quote: Ubuntu Desktop 22.04 or 20.04 LTS with a GNOME graphical desktop environment is required for enrollment. Linux devices enrolled with Microsoft Intune are considered corporate-owned devices, and device enrollment isn't supported with personal devices.

claim: Belgian eID middleware is officially packaged for Linux (Debian/Ubuntu and RPM based systems) via the eID-archive package.
quote: You can install the eID software on Linux by installing the 'eID-archive' package, which enables the eID package repositories.

claim: Kernel anti-cheat such as Easy Anti-Cheat and BattlEye blocks Linux unless the game developer explicitly enables support.
quote: many anti-cheat systems such as Easy Anti-Cheat and BattlEye rely on kernel-level monitoring and often block Linux environments entirely.

claim: Azure Data Studio retired 28 Feb 2026; Microsoft points users to VS Code with the MSSQL extension.
quote: Azure Data Studio retired on February 28, 2026 and is no longer supported... Microsoft recommends migrating to Visual Studio Code with the MSSQL extension.

claim: Canonical maintains a searchable certified-hardware catalogue; certification runs 500+ OS compatibility tests on the exact model.
quote: Certified devices are tested for reliability and performance... an extensive set of over 500 OS compatibility focused hardware tests.

claim: Successful 2026 switchers treated the move as a tool-selection problem, inventorying daily apps into native / alternative / no-equivalent buckets.
quote: identifying exactly which applications they use daily, finding that some have native Linux versions, some have credible alternatives, and some don't have Linux equivalents.
